Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

replace verb

take the place of

also take the place of, take over from, succeed someone, stand in for, successor

classical

Quint. 2.2.5: succēdere sē in eōrum locum … exīstimet
Caes. BG 5.16 (Lewis & Short): ut integrī et recentēs dēfatīgātīs succēderent

succēdō, succēdere, successī, successum

verb, third conjugation, intransitive; with the dative, or in locum and the genitive

take the place of, take over from, succeed

Lewis & Short: “to follow, follow after, take the place of, relieve”. A successor is successor (Ov. Met. 3.589).

Other words

  • sufficiō, sufficere, suffēcī, suffectum — appoint (someone) in another’s place

    verb, third conjugation (-iō); with in locum and the genitive · also used · classical · M-O s.v. replace (someone): in alicujus locum sufficī

    Lewis & Short: “to choose or elect in the place of any one (class.; esp. freq. of magistrates)”: a consul elected in place of one who has died is cōnsul suffectus.

  • vice (alicujus) fungī — act in place of, stand in for

    phrase; fungor with the ablative · also used · classical · Hor. Ars 304: ergō fungar vice cōtis

  • locum (alicujus) ūsurpāre — take someone’s place

    avoid · modern · Traupman 22: locum mātris meae numquam ūsurpāre potest

    Lewis & Short give ūsurpāre as “to make use of, to take possession of”, but not with locum in this sense; say in locum alicujus succēdere.

Examples

  • sūmat igitur ante omnia parentis ergā discipulōs suōs animum, ac succēdere sē in eōrum locum, ā quibus sibi līberī trādantur, exīstimet

    Let him first of all take on a parent’s feelings towards his pupils, and think of himself as taking the place of those who hand their children over to him.Quint. 2.2.5

  • quippe et Rhō litterae, quā Dēmosthenēs quoque labōrāvit, Labda succēdit

    for Lambda takes the place of the letter Rho, which even Demosthenes had trouble withQuint. 1.11.5

  • interdum fessae succēdit laeva sorōrī alternatque vicēs

    Now and then the left hand takes over from her tired sister, and they take turns.Mor. 28–29

  • locum alicujus ūsurpāre

    to take someone’s placeTraupman 360

See also replace, in turn, follow.
